thread:
rachel: Hey team — customer acme-analytics on dedicated/VPC (us-west-2) started seeing 401s after a gateway cert rotation. They report Authorization and X-Rd-User headers disappearing between their edge proxy -> NLB -> our Istio ingress. Repro steps and logs below.

kevin: Can you drop a minimal curl repro and confirm whether TLS is terminated before reaching istio-ingress? :eyes: 

rachel: Repro (customer confirmed):
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Rd-User: alice@acme.com\" https://dedicated.acme.internal/v1/predict
```
Response: 401. Our ingress logs show no Authorization header in the request context.

sophia: Important detail: in some Istio/Gateway setups we sanitize unknown headers by default. If they recently changed any Gateway header filters or an Envoy config, that could drop Authorization unless whitelisted. Also check proxy_protocol between NLB and istio-ingress.

omid: Another angle — if there's an intermediate HAProxy/re-encryptor it might be moving Authorization into a Proxy-Authorization header or converting JWT -> opaque cookie. Need the full ingress access log and the pre-ingress (edge) logs.

rachel: Scrubbed envoy access log from our ingress when customer hit the endpoint:
```
[2026-03-10T17:42:01Z] "GET /v1/predict HTTP/1.1" 401 - "-" "10.0.2.5" "-" header x-rd-user: -
```
Note the header is missing.

support-marc: Customer mentioned Okta token scopes disappearing too. If Authorization is present at the NLB but missing at ingress, check target group type (instance vs ip) and whether the NLB has proxy protocol enabled — that can change how Envoy treats incoming headers.

eng-infra-bot: deploy completed for istio-gateway v1.17.3-rc (hash abc123) :rocket:

kevin: Quick debug checklist: 1) ask customer to curl our internal ingress IP (bypass edge) to confirm headers are preserved, 2) confirm NLB listeners are TLS passthrough vs terminate, 3) inspect Gateway resource for `headers.request.remove`/`add` rules and any `header_to_metadata` filters.

sophia: Workaround we can try on our side: enable explicit header whitelist in the dedicated-gateway Helm values so Envoy doesn't strip Authorization/X-Rd-* headers. Example values snippet:
```
gateway:
  extraEnvoyConfig:
    header_whitelist:
      - Authorization
      - X-Rd-User
      - X-Rd-Auth
    preserve_external_auth_headers: true
```
Apply to a canary gateway and test.

omid: Also verify whether the customer recently enabled `connection: close` on their edge proxy — we've seen some proxies rewrite or drop hop-by-hop headers when that changes. Packet capture (tcpdump) at the NLB target could be telling.

rachel: Customer confirmed they run an HAProxy re-encryptor in front and they rotated it right before the incident. They also confirmed: direct curl to the internal ingress IP returns 200 and shows Authorization header present. So pipeline is: client -> HAProxy -> NLB -> istio-ingress; issue must be between HAProxy and NLB.

kevin: If direct to ingress works, then a canary Helm patch to our gateway to explicitly allow the headers is reasonable. But long term, the right fix is to instruct the customer to preserve headers across their HAProxy stage or set the NLB to TLS passthrough. For immediate mitigation I'll prepare a canary patch that adds the whitelist and a deployment plan + rollback.

sophia: I can open the PR with the Helm patch and rollout steps. Suggest annotation approach so we can toggle per-dedicated cluster: `redwood.io/allow-external-auth: "true"`. Patch steps:
1) update values.yaml for dedicated cluster
2) `helm upgrade --reuse-values --set gateway.extraEnvoyConfig.header_whitelist={Authorization,X-Rd-User,X-Rd-Auth} dedicated-gateway .`
3) `kubectl rollout restart deployment/istio-ingress -n redwood-gateway` (limit to canary nodes via nodeSelector)
4) smoke test with direct and edge path

kevin: I'll stage the canary and keep traffic low. Also add an alert rule to watch for spike in 401s > 5% in the dedicated cluster.

rachel: Scheduling a customer call at 18:00 UTC to repro with us and test the canary. I'll collect NLB access logs and packet captures before the call.

support-marc: Note: if they use signed cookies -> auth conversion on the mid-proxy, token scopes may be lost during conversion. Ask them to include an example request/response trace from their HAProxy logs.

omid: Small note — if proxy_protocol is enabled, Envoy's listener needs `use_proxy_proto: true`. If not set, source addr/header parsing may be wrong and some header filters behave unexpectedly.

kevin: After the canary patch we should also run a quick regression test: edge -> NLB -> ingress -> application, compare headers at each hop. If it looks clean, promote to full rollout. I'll also prepare rollback `helm rollback` steps.

rachel: Thanks — I'll coordinate with the customer and update after the 18:00 call. Tagging @support-oncall for monitoring during the window. :eyes: 

support-oncall: Noted. I'll stand by and attach an alert if 401 error rate crosses threshold. :thumbsup:

kevin: Thanks team. Please keep packet captures and ingress/access logs in the incident folder for postmortem.

rachel: Will do. Updating ticket with next steps and the canary PR link once it's up.
